title: Orbital Velocity of a Satellite

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Gravitation

explanation: Orbital velocity is the speed needed to maintain a stable circular orbit at radius r, found by equating gravitational force to the required centripetal force: GMm/r² = mvo²/r. Orbital velocity DECREASES with increasing orbital radius (higher/farther satellites move slower), and at any given radius, vo = ve/√2 — always smaller than the escape velocity at that same radius.

variables.meaning: Mass of the central body (e.g. Earth)
Orbital radius (from the centre of the central body)

workedExample.scenario: A satellite orbits Earth just above the surface (r ≈ R ≈ 6.4×10⁶ m, g ≈ 9.8 m/s²).

commonMistakes: Using the planet's radius R when the satellite orbits at a much larger radius r above the surface — r must be measured from the centre of the planet to the satellite's actual orbit, not just the surface radius.
Confusing orbital velocity with escape velocity — they are related by a fixed factor of √2 at the same radius but represent different physical situations.
genZNote: Orbital velocity is escape velocity's more chill sibling — always exactly √2 times slower.
